paper.title: Statistically Robust, Risk-Averse Best Arm Identification in Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-aware fixed-budget best arm identification with distribution-oblivious (statistically robust) algorithms
unmapped: Arm objective is xi_1*E[X] + xi_2*CVaR_alpha(X) (risk-aware, loss minimization) with known weights xi_1, xi_2 and CVaR level alpha
Only condition C1: E|X|^p < infinity for some unknown p>1; moment bounds (p,B,V) are NOT known to the learner (distribution oblivious)
settings.definition_quote: Given a fixed budget of $T$ arm pulls in total, our goal is to identify the arm that minimizes $\obj(i) = \xi_{1} \Exp{X(i)} + \xi_{2}\calp(X(i)),$ where $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ are non-negative (and given) weights. This places us in the \emph{fixed budget, pure exploration} framework.

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-aware fixed-budget best arm identification, two arms (lower bound)
unmapped: Arm objective is xi_1*E[X] + xi_2*CVaR_alpha(X) with known weights
Arm distributions satisfy only C1 (some p>1 moment finite); class M of all such instances
settings.definition_quote: Let $K = 2,$ and consider an algorithm $\pi$ that is consistent over $\M.$

algorithms.name: Successive rejects with truncation-based mean and CVaR estimators
Successive rejects with median-of-bins (median-of-means / median-of-cvars) estimators
SR-type algorithms with empirical mean/CVaR estimators

conditions: nu_1 and nu_2 mutually absolutely continuous

source.label: lower-bound-non-obl-theorem
source.quote:
Let $K = 2.$ Consider a bandit instance $
u = (
u_1, 
u_2) \in \M$ satisfying $\obj(1) 
eq \obj(2),$ such that $
u_1$ and $
u_2$ are mutually absolutely continuous. Any algorithm~$\pi$ that is consistent over $\{(
u_1,
u_2),(
u_2,
u_1)\}$ satisfies \limsup_{T 	o \infty} - rac{1}{T} \log p_e(
u,\pi, T) \leq \max (	ext{KL}(
u_1, 
u_2), 	ext{KL}(
u_2, 
u_1)).

results.notes: Bound is on the error exponent: limsup of -(1/T) log p_e is at most the expression, i.e. p_e cannot decay faster than exp(-T*max KL). Extension of Audibert et al. 2010 to mean-CVaR objective.

conditions: algorithm consistent over the class M of all instances satisfying C1
nu_1 (optimal arm) is regularly varying with index a > 1

source.label: fund-lower-bound-theorem
source.quote:
Let $K = 2,$ and consider an algorithm $\pi$ that is consistent over $\M.$ For any bandit instance $
u = (
u_1, 
u_2)$ satisfying $\obj(1) < \obj(2),$ such that $
u_1$ is a regularly varying distribution with index $a>1$, \lim_{T 	o \infty} - rac{1}{T} \log p_e(
u,\pi, T) = 0.

results.notes: Error exponent equals zero: the error probability of any statistically robust algorithm decays slower than exponentially in T on such instances.

symbols.a: Pareto tail index of the optimal arm, a > 1

conditions: any SR-type algorithm using empirical (mean/CVaR) estimators
arm 1 optimal with Pareto(x_m, a) distribution, a > 1
arm 2 is a constant with obj(2) = obj(1) + Delta

source.quote:
Consider a two-arm instance $
u = (
u_1, 
u_2).$ Arm~1 is optimal and has a $\mathrm{Pareto}(x_m,a)$ distribution with $a>1.$ Arm~2 is a constant having a value such that $\obj(2) = \obj(1) + \Delta.$ The probability of error, $p_e$, of any SR-type algorithm using empirical estimators is bounded below by $ rac{C}{T^{a-1}} + o\left( rac{1}{T^{a-1}}ight),$ where $C > 0$ is an instance (and algorithm) dependent constant.

results.notes: Stated as C/T^{a-1} + o(1/T^{a-1}); recorded as Omega. Proof omitted in paper.

symbols.Delta_obj_i: gap in the mean-CVaR objective of the i-th best arm, obj[i]-obj[1] (ordered)
symbols.q_m: truncation exponent for mean estimator, b_m(n)=n^{q_m}
symbols.q_c: truncation exponent for CVaR estimator, b_c(n)=n^{q_c}
symbols.n_star: max((12 xi_1 B/Delta[2])^{1/(q_m min(p-1,1))}, (8 xi_2 B/(beta Delta[2]))^{1/(q_c(p-1))}, (B/min(alpha,beta))^{1/(q_c p)})

conditions: arms satisfy C1 with E|X|^p < B, p in (1,2]
tuning: successive rejects phase lengths n_k = (T-K)/((K+1-k) logbar(K))

source.label: sr-prob-of-error-tea
source.quote: Let the arms satisfy the condition \textbf{C1}. The probability of incorrect arm identification for the successive rejects algorithm using truncation based estimators is bounded as follows. p_{e} \leq \sum_{i=2}^{K} (K+1-i) 2\text{exp}(...) + \sum_{i=2}^{K} (K+1-i) 6\text{exp}(...) for $T> K+K\overline{\log}(K)n^{*},$ ...

results.notes: With q_m=q, q_c=q/2 this gives O(exp(-gamma T^{1-q})). Algorithm is distribution oblivious; the threshold depends on unknown B, p, Delta[2].

symbols.q_m: bin-size exponent for median-of-means, N_m = n_k^{q_m}
symbols.q_c: bin-size exponent for median-of-cvars, N_c = n_k^{q_c}
symbols.T_star_inst: instance-dependent horizon threshold (depends on p, B, V, Delta[2], xi_1, xi_2, beta)

conditions: arms satisfy C1 (p in (1,2] for the explicit threshold)

source.label: sr-prob-of-error-mob
source.quote: Let the arms satisfy the condition \textbf{C1}. The probability of incorrect arm identification for the successive rejects algorithm using median-of-bins estimators is bounded as follows p_e \leq \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} k [ \exp(-\frac{1}{8}(\frac{T-K}{\overline{\log}(K)(K+1-k)})^{1-q_m}) + \exp(-\frac{1}{8}(\frac{T-K}{\overline{\log}(K)(K+1-k)})^{1-q_c}) ] for $T>T^{*},$ where $T^*$ is a instance-dependent threshold.

results.notes: With q_c=q_m=q, p_e = O(exp(-gamma T^{1-q})). Gaps enter only through the threshold T*.
